failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial. The docs worked well for this task: the 'Which processor should I use?' section points flat attribute/class edits to WP_HTML_Tag_Processor; the Usage/Finding tags sections document construction with new WP_HTML_Tag_Processor($html), next_tag('img'), and forward scanning; next_tag() explicitly says tag matching is ASCII case-insensitive, tag-like text in comments is not matched, and incomplete trailing tags are not modified; add_class() explicitly says it creates class when absent and appends without removing or reordering existing classes; get_updated_html() is documented as the correct way to return queued edits while preserving untouched bytes. Near-miss: the add_class() method section documents class-list semantics clearly, but the exact placement/serialization of a newly created class attribute is easier to infer from broader attribute-update docs than from add_class() itself.

doc_gaps.problem: The method explains class creation and append/no-duplicate semantics, but does not locally state how a newly created class attribute is positioned and serialized relative to existing attributes.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short sentence that class attribute creation follows normal added-attribute ordering/serialization rules and preserves all untouched attributes byte-for-byte.
